newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan deploys 60 patrol boats against isle protest.
newsitem.headline: Japan deploys 60 patrol boats against isle protest.

text.p: The Japanese coastguard deployed about 60 patrol boats on Monday to prevent a flotilla of about 20 protest vessels from Taiwan approaching a disputed island chain in the East China Sea, coastguard sources said.

A spokesman for Japan's coastguard, the Maritime Safety Agency, said activists aboard several protest boats started fishing on Monday morning in waters about 37 km (23 miles) away from the islands, which are called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese.
"As of 7.30 a.m. (2230 GMT Sunday) about 20 boats were sailing closer to the Senkaku islands," the spokesman said. "We are warning them not to enter Japan's territorial waters."
Japan claims territorial waters extending 12 nautical miles around the islands.

The spokesman said there had been no reports of any clashes between coastguards and the activists, who have pledged to carry out what they have dubbed the "Diaoyu Island World Cup Fishing Contest", a protest designed to challenge Japan's sovereignty by violating its waters.
Coastguard sources said the agency mobilised about 60 patrol boats, some of them armed, to prevent the protesters from entering Japan's territorial waters.
The coastguard spokesman said none of the protesters had tried to pierce the coastguard cordon.
"It has been calm so far. We really hope they will finish their activities quietly," he said.
The activists have said they would not rule out a landing on the cluster of uninhabited islands, which lie 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Taiwan, and are claimed by Japan, Taiwan and China.
The dispute over sovereignty has ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse there in July 1996.
Japan took over the islands as war booty after defeating imperial China in 1895. China and Taiwan say they should have been returned after Japan's defeat in World War Two.
Some 20 activists from Hong Kong were due to link up with the flotilla off Taiwan's coast later on Monday.
